newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: U.S. AMWAY SETS ITS SIGHTS ON AFRICA.
newsitem.headline: U.S. AMWAY SETS ITS SIGHTS ON AFRICA.

text.p: After sweeping through South East Asia, U.S. direct selling giant Amway Corporation has set it sights on Africa and planned to launch in South Africa in August, country manager Peter Beaumont said on Thursday.
"The South African launch is the start of the move through Africa," he told Reuters.
The group's range of homecare, health food and cosmetic products would initially be imported from the U.S. although promotional material and stationery would be sourced locally.

"We only have manufacturing plants in the U.S., Korea and China and the economy of scale that we get in the U.S. means that even with the duty rates, this will be competitive in South Africa," he said.
Products would be sold by "several thousand" local distributors hand-picked by sponsors, some of which would be South Africans now operating in other countries.
Each distributor would have to buy a sales kit, which would be sold for between 300 and 400 rand but Beaumont said it would not be a pyramid scheme.
The South African office would be in Cape Town and its warehouse in Johannesburg.
Amway has built up a strong presence in South East Asia and Japan in recent years. It recently moved into the Philippines.
It is the second U.S. direct mail company to move into South Africa. The first was Avon Products Inc, which last year bought Justine Pty as a conduit for its cosmetics range.
